name: Seawinds Garden
reason: Rule 1: still only one agency listing and no visitor source describing a draw beyond a local council garden; short stop.

name: Coastal Walk (Mornington Peninsula)
reason: Rules 1-3: Parks Victoria's national park page promotes it as the two-day clifftop Coastal Walk through ocean beaches; a named multi-day walk like Hump Ridge. Objection: single agency source, part of the national park; but a linear route is its own draw.

name: Greens Bush
reason: Rule 1/3: Parks Victoria names it as the kangaroo haven and largest native bushland on the peninsula. For: distinct wildlife and tracks, inland from coast sections. Against: a section of Mornington Peninsula National Park, one source.

name: Mushroom Reef Marine Sanctuary
reason: Rules 1-3: Parks Victoria lists the sanctuary at Flinders Ocean Beach for rockpooling and snorkelling; second-tier natural stop. Objection: one source, landslip advisory nearby.

name: Sorrento Front Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage singles out Sorrento's calm bay beach beside the ocean beach; second-tier beach stop. Objection: one source, ordinary bay beach.

name: Fingal Beach
reason: Rule 3: Parks Victoria mentions it only as a picnic/beach access within Mornington Peninsula National Park alongside the Fingal and Coppins tracks; ordinary beach, part of the park, no distinct draw named.

name: Cheviot Beach
reason: Rule 3/2: Parks Victoria (Point Nepean) only has a viewing area and memorial overlooking the beach (Holt disappearance, SS Cheviot wreck) on the Cheviot Hill walk; part of Point Nepean spot and a hazardous beach not visited itself.

name: Portsea
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage names Portsea's foreshore pub, sunset and back beach; Parks Victoria lists Portsea Surf Beach; harbour/beach village at the peninsula tip. Objection: one town source, overlaps Point Nepean NP.

name: Western Port
reason: Rule 3: a large bay, not one place to visit; its draws are listed as individual spots (Rhyll, French Island, Churchill Island).

name: McCrae Homestead
reason: Rules 1-2: National Trust page confirms a public heritage homestead with entry charge ($15 adult, last entry 3pm) and Parks Victoria/Wikivoyage listing. Objection: small house, limited open days.

name: Alba Thermal Springs & Spa
reason: Rules 1-3: Australian Traveller and others cover a 15 ha thermal springs complex with 31 pools, a paid day-visit attraction like Peninsula Hot Springs. Objection: new commercial spa, premium price.

name: Mornington
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage calls it the peninsula's largest town with a long main street running to the beach and pier; a harbour town a guide recommends. Objection: one source, generic town.

name: Mornington Railway
reason: Rule 4/2: heritage trains run only on the first three Sundays of each month between Moorooduc and Mornington; the ride is the attraction and operates as a scheduled occasion, not a place available whenever one arrives.

name: Dromana Beach
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage highlights the beach lined with brightly painted boat sheds; a recognisable photo stop. Objection: one source.

name: Bridgewater Bay
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage names Blairgowrie's Bridgewater Bay for rock pools safe for swimming at low tide. For: a named natural feature. Against: single source, tide-dependent, local beach.

name: Red Hill Cheese
reason: Rule 2/1: a single producer's cellar door, open weekends and public holidays only; not a distinct attraction.

name: A Maze'N Things
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage lists a daily family attraction (maze averaging 45 min, mini-golf, ropes course, illusions hall) with entry fee. Objection: one source, kids' commercial attraction, older listing.

name: Phillip Island Chocolate Factory
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage describes a long-visit attraction with the world's largest chocolate waterfall and interactive displays, open daily. Objection: one source, part retail.

name: Purple Hen Wines
reason: Rule 2/3: an individual winery cellar door; Wikivoyage lists it but no distinct attraction beyond tasting.

name: Rhyll Inlet and Conservation Hill
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage and Visit Phillip Island both describe boardwalks through Ramsar-listed mangroves and a Conservation Hill observation tower with birdlife. Objection: modest birdwatching stop.

name: Fairhaven Northern Beach Walk
reason: Rule 3: a track on French Island, part of the larger island spot; single agency source.

name: Old Coast Road Track
reason: Rule 3: a track on French Island, part of the larger island spot; single agency source.

name: West Coast Wetlands Walking Track
reason: Rule 3: a track on French Island, part of the larger island spot; single agency source.

name: Bunurong Marine National Park
reason: Rules 1-3: Parks Victoria and Visit Gippsland both promote rockpooling on intertidal platforms, snorkelling, Eagles Nest rock stack and the Bunurong Coastal Drive. Objection: tide-dependent, hazardous beaches.

name: Inverloch Surf Beach
reason: Rule 3: Parks Victoria names Inverloch's patrolled beach only as part of the town; near-duplicate of Inverloch.

name: Inverloch
reason: Rules 1-3: Parks Victoria and Visit Gippsland name it as the well-serviced town with visitor centre, patrolled beach, Screw Creek walk and Townsend Bluff lookout, and base for Bunurong coast and dinosaur fossil coast. Objection: Wikivoyage page is a stub.

name: Shack Bay
reason: Rule 3: a clifftop car park and beach inside Bunurong Marine National Park (Parks Victoria names it only as a snorkel/dive access point); part of the park spot.

name: Undertow Bay
reason: Rule 3: western end of Bunurong Marine National Park, mentioned only as a boundary point; part of the park spot.

name: Cape Paterson Surf Beach
reason: Rule 3: Parks Victoria mentions the patrolled beach only as the western end of the Cape Paterson-Inverloch coast; near-duplicate of the coast/Bunurong spot.

name: Cape Paterson
reason: Rule 3: Parks Victoria and Visit Gippsland name it as the coastal hamlet where the Bunurong Coastal Drive begins, with no distinct see/do of its own; Wikivoyage page is a stub.

name: Woodside Beach
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage page is an empty stub and no tourism or Parks Victoria source found naming it as a visitor stop on a long Ninety Mile Beach stretch.
